NM-senate.statusNote: Sen. Ben Ray Lujan (D) won the June 2 primary 84-16 over Matt Dodson; Larry Marker (R) of Roswell won the GOP nomination as a write-in with 4,470 votes (threshold 2,351) after no Republican filed for the ballot.

NM-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. Lujan Grisham term-limited): former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland (D, 72% primary win) faces former Rio Rancho Mayor Gregg Hull (R, 47% in a three-way primary). Independent Ken Miyagishima was denied ballot access, dropped out, and endorsed Hull.

candidates.name: Ben Ray Lujan
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2021, seeking a second term; previously represented New Mexico's 3rd district in the House (2009-2021), rising to Assistant Speaker. Before Congress he chaired the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission. Won the June 2 Democratic primary 84-16 over Matt Dodson.
priorities: Lower costs and affordable health care

cost.label: Cosponsored the Raise the Wage Act to lift the federal minimum wage and phase out the tipped subminimum wage: 'New Mexico's workers want to receive a fair day's pay for a fair day's work' (Los Alamos Daily Post)

taxes.label: Voted Yea on H.R. 5376, the Inflation Reduction Act reconciliation bill financed by a new 15% corporate minimum tax, which passed 51-50 (Senate roll call vote 325)

education.label: Sees schools as 'centers of the community that provide wraparound services, including mental and behavioral health services' (Senate office issues page)

health.label: Longtime public-option advocate: 'we must demand a public option' in health reform (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Voted Nay on S. 5, the Laken Riley Act requiring DHS to detain immigrants charged with theft; it passed 64-35 (Senate roll call vote 7, 119th Congress)

climate.label: Mixed record: supports the Green New Deal and authored clean-energy bills, but joined Republicans in 2021 to block a hydraulic fracturing ban (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Co-sponsored the Women's Health Protection Act of 2025 to restore nationwide abortion access: 'we will keep fighting to restore and protect reproductive rights' (Sen. Lujan press release)

democracy.label: Introduced the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, Freedom to Vote Act, and Native American Voting Rights Act; opposes the SAVE Act as 'anti-voter' (Sen. Lujan press release)

safety.label: Voted yea both on the First Step Act's sentencing and reentry reforms in the House, 358-36, and on the enforcement-side HALT Fentanyl Act permanently placing fentanyl-related substances in Schedule I, 84-16 (House Clerk roll call 448, Senate roll call 127)

candidates.name: Larry Marker
candidates.now: Businessman (oil and gas, farming, ranching, construction)
candidates.background: Roswell businessman whose career spans oil and gas production, farming, ranching, manufacturing, and construction; self-described 'America First' conservative. Ran for state land commissioner in 2022 and the state Senate in 2024, losing both. Won the Republican U.S. Senate nomination as a write-in with 4,470 votes after no Republican filed for the ballot.
priorities: New Mexico energy independence (oil, gas, hydrogen, nuclear)
Secure the border and shut down the fentanyl pipeline
Stop regulatory overreach on farmers, ranchers, and small businesses

cost.label: Wants to loosen regulations 'hurting small businesses'; says Lujan pushes 'welfare-type programs' instead of economic opportunity through capitalism (Santa Fe New Mexican)

immigration.label: Backs President Trump's immigration policies; 'shut down the fentanyl pipeline' and 'support Border Patrol' (Santa Fe New Mexican; campaign site)

climate.label: 'Make New Mexico a leader in oil, gas, hydrogen, and nuclear innovation'; campaign built on energy independence and pushing back on regulation (campaign site)

safety.label: 'The first duty of government is to keep its citizens safe': opposes 'policies that shield violent offenders' and backs 'Border Patrol and local law enforcement' (campaign site)

candidates.name: Deb Haaland
candidates.now: Former U.S. Secretary of the Interior (2021-2025)
candidates.background: Former U.S. Secretary of the Interior (2021-2025), the first Native American Cabinet secretary, and an enrolled member of Laguna Pueblo. Represented New Mexico's 1st district in the U.S. House (2019-2021) and chaired the state Democratic Party. Won the June 2 Democratic primary 72-28 over Attorney General Sam Bregman.
priorities: Affordability agenda: raise the minimum wage, crack down on price gouging
Fix the doctor shortage and expand rural health care
Build more housing and ban rent fixing

cost.label: Raise the state minimum wage and 'crack down on big industries that price gouge at the cost of every day New Mexicans' (campaign site)

health.label: Supported Medicare for All in Congress; as governor would fill Medicaid gaps with budget surpluses and expand the Health Care Affordability Fund (Wikipedia; campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed approach: 'aggressively build more housing' by reducing barriers and expediting permitting, while banning landlords from using AI algorithms that inflate rents and expanding down payment assistance (campaign site)

immigration.label: Would limit state coordination with ICE, require agents to identify themselves, and create 500-yard ICE-free zones around schools: 'the state is the first line of defense' (Native News Online)

climate.label: Progressive who supports the Green New Deal; her campaign was endorsed by the climate action group Sunrise Movement (Wikipedia)

education.label: Community school models with counseling and school-based health care, bolstering universal childcare, and expanding the Opportunity Scholarship to free tuition including graduate education (campaign site)

safety.label: Office of Community Safety pairing social workers with responders, substance-abuse treatment 'beyond incarceration', violence-intervention programs, plus new tech for police (campaign site)

repro.label: 'Fierce and unwavering advocate for reproductive freedom'; collected signatures to repeal New Mexico's dormant criminal abortion ban (Planned Parenthood Votes NM endorsement)

democracy.label: Voted Yea on H.R. 1, the For the People Act, with automatic voter registration and expanded early and mail voting; it passed 234-193 (House Clerk roll call 118, 2019)

nullNotes.taxes: checked campaign plans page (child tax credit increase is a targeted household measure that does not fit the axis), Ballotpedia, and Wikipedia, nothing documented; roll-call/record search also empty

candidates.name: Gregg Hull
candidates.background: Longest-serving mayor in Rio Rancho history, leading New Mexico's third-largest city from 2014 to 2026; former small-business owner and past chairman of the New Mexico Mayors Caucus. Touts $6 billion in investment attracted to Rio Rancho and 12 national budget awards. Won the June 2 Republican primary with 47% over Doug Turner (37%) and Duke Rodriguez (16%).
priorities: Public safety: more police, zero tolerance for violent crime
Border security to end the fentanyl crisis

cost.label: Regulatory reform plan: cut red tape and the 'long, confusing licensing rules that make it harder to move, start a job, or open a small business' (campaign site)

education.label: Will 'make meaningful investments in public education and demand accountability', with youth tutoring, stronger special education, and expanded Career Technical Education (campaign issues page)

democracy.label: 'Gregg will fight for statewide Voter ID laws that protect legally registered voters' (campaign election integrity page)

health.label: Market-side cost fixes: 'reform medical malpractice laws to reduce costs', lower prescription drug prices, strengthen rural hospitals (campaign site)

immigration.label: 'Enhance border security to end the fentanyl crisis' (campaign site)

taxes.label: Fiscal restraint record: 12 years without raising Rio Rancho's sales tax rate, budgets that live 'within our means' (Source New Mexico)

climate.label: 'Expanding the state's energy portfolio to include all sources while unleashing our oil and gas operations' (campaign site)

safety.label: Doubled Rio Rancho's police budget; pledges to 'increase police presence throughout the state' and a 'zero-tolerance policy for all violent crimes and crimes against children' (campaign site)

housing.label: As mayor oversaw 7,200 new single-family homes with city infrastructure support for the Los Diamantes master-planned development, while completing affordable housing projects and backing a city affordable housing study, 'a comprehensive study will verify our needs' (City Desk ABQ, KRQE)
